title: Secure audit forwarder protocol and SIEM compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our current audit log delivery model provides basic webhook delivery and retry semantics, but lacks a standardized forwarder protocol that guarantees secure, ordered, and auditable delivery to external SIEM endpoints (Splunk HTTP Event Collector, Datadog Logs, generic syslog/CEF collectors) while respecting RBAC v2 scoping and PII redaction policies. This ticket defines and implements a "secure audit forwarder" (SAF) protocol and SIEM compatibility layer to improve delivery guarantees, testability, and operational visibility.

Goals:
- Define a bidirectional handshake and acknowledgement protocol for audit sinks (ACK, NACK, transient backoff instructions).
- Support idempotent event delivery using delivery-id and sequence tokens to preserve per-tenant ordering when requested.
- Implement pluggable connector adapters for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs HTTP, and generic syslog/CEF.
- Ensure compatibility with RBAC v2 scoping: forwarder will filter and tag events by tenant/role, apply dynamic redaction rules, and attach signed metadata indicating the applied policy version.
- Preserve end-to-end confidentiality: support payload encryption-at-rest and in-flight using customer KMS keys and signed delivery tokens.
- Provide a controlled backfill workflow and safe replays for customer-requested historical exports with strict audit trail.
- Expose observability: per-connector metrics (latency, inflight, retry count), delivery success rate, SLA breach alerts, and a debug webhook sink for engineering.

Non-Goals:
- No attempt here to replace existing audit schema; this ticket focuses on transport and guarantees. Schema changes will be separate.

Design highlights:
- Handshake: connector registers with control-plane using TLS client cert; control-plane issues a short-lived bearer token and connector-id. Connectors and control-plane exchange supported ack modes: at_least_once (default), exactly_once (best-effort with idempotency token), best_effort (fire-and-forget for low-priority telemetry).
- Delivery semantics: each audit bundle includes (delivery_id, tenant_id, sequence_window_start, sequence_window_end, policy_version, optional-encryption-key-id). The forwarder persists unacked bundles in a per-connector durable queue (encrypted). Retries use exponential backoff with jitter; permanent NACKs move bundles to a configurable DLQ.
- Ordering: where tenant policy requests strict ordering, forwarder will stream single-tenant sequences through a pinned worker that preserves order; where cost/throughput trumps ordering, we allow unordered parallelism.
- Idempotency: connectors must echo receipt with delivery_id and last_sequence_ack; control-plane deduplicates using a short-term index keyed by (tenant_id, delivery_id).
- Backfill/replay: backfills are initiated via Console or API; they create a replay job with immutable audit export snapshot, tenant-scoped, and require admin SSO approval and audit trail entry.
- RBAC + privacy: before forwarding, events are filtered by RBAC v2 rules and redaction policies. A policy_version header is attached and cryptographically signed. Admin controls can opt connectors into different redaction levels.
- Compatibility adapters: implement adapter interface with transformation and best-effort batching. Provide templates for Splunk HEC (JSON batching, X-SF-ACK header support), Datadog (Logs intake v1 with API key rotation), and Syslog (RFC5424).

Operational controls and runbook:
- Canary rollout: start with internal-only Splunk workspace, enable per-tenant canary buckets, monitor delivery_success_rate >= 99.9% and median latency < 500ms.
- Metrics: connector.delivery.success, connector.delivery.failure, connector.retry.count, connector.queue.depth, connector.dlq.size, connector.last_ack_lag.
- Alerting: page on dlq growth > 1000 events in 1h or connector.last_ack_lag > 10m for >3 connectors.
- Playbook: how to restart connector, rehydrate queue from durable store, perform a safe replay, and revoke connector tokens.

Implementation plan and phases:
1) Spec and adapter contracts (this ticket): finalize wire format, handshake, ack modes, and adapter interface.
2) Core forwarder service: durable per-connector queues, ack processing, retry engine, DLQ.
3) Adapters: Splunk HEC, Datadog, Syslog.
4) RBAC integration: policy fetch + redaction hooks, signature of policy_version.
5) Console + API: connector onboarding flow, token rotation UI, backfill initiation.
6) Canary and metrics rollout, followed by broad customer opt-in.

Rollout constraints: Must pass security review for key management and token lifecycle (see security_review_required). We will gate exactly_once mode behind Dedicated customers initially due to stronger SLAs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Handshake protocol documented and reviewed; sample client implemented for Splunk HEC.
2) Forwarder persists unacked bundles; retry engine respects per-connector policy.
3) Idempotency works for repeated delivery_id within retention window; duplicates do not reach sinks.
4) RBAC v2 filter + redaction applied prior to forwarding; policy_version attached and verifiable.
5) Metrics emitted and dashboard in Console; alerts configured.
6) Backfill job can be requested from Console and replayed to a test connector with full audit trail recorded.
comments: 2025-11-05: Initial proposal written by Aisha. Shared with Security and Infra for review.
2025-11-12: Marco prototyped durable queue using RocksDB-backed store; early perf looks promising.
2025-12-02: Security requested KMS envelope encryption for connector queues and token rotation policy (see related link).
2026-01-18: Spike testing Splunk HEC batching modes: single-event vs. batch-of-500 — batch reduces token cost but increases worst-case latency.
2026-02-09: Decision: default ack mode remains at_least_once; exactly_once is opt-in for Dedicated tenants due to additional state requirements.
2026-03-10: Integration test harness added for Datadog adapter; test failures surfaced around API key rotation handling. Marco assigned to fix.
2026-03-12: Security review prereq checklist completed; requesting formal security sign-off and canary window scheduling.
